projects.name: MediSync
projects.tagline: AI-driven national healthcare platform for Sri Lanka
projects.role: Solo project: I designed and built all three services.
projects.problem: Patients, doctors, pharmacies, hospitals and labs need to share medical records and prescriptions safely, and health officials need early warning when a disease starts to spread in a district.
projects.solution: A three-service platform: a React 19 front end, a Node.js / Express 5 API and a Python Flask ML engine. Each role has its own portal, patient records sit behind encryption and OTP-based consent, and a public map shows outbreak risk for every district in Sri Lanka.
highlights: Outbreak forecasting with Prophet and ARIMA, plus z-score anomaly detection for unusual case spikes.
Public Sri Lanka district choropleth map built with Leaflet and GeoJSON.
AES-256 field-level encryption with blind indexes, keys in HashiCorp Vault, Redis, OTP-gated access to patient records and audit logs.
Separate portals for patients, doctors, pharmacies, hospitals/labs and admins.
Drug-interaction and allergy checks against 3,000 drugs, 191k+ interaction pairs and 71k+ ICD codes.
CI/CD with GitHub Actions, deployed on Vercel.
impact: Cut the initial JavaScript bundle from 465 KB to 145 KB with code-splitting.
cvBullets: Designed and built, solo, a three-service healthcare platform (React 19, Node.js/Express 5, Python Flask, MongoDB Atlas) with role-based portals for patients, doctors, pharmacies, hospitals/labs and admins.
Built an outbreak-forecasting engine in Flask using Prophet, ARIMA and z-score anomaly detection, feeding a public district-level risk map of Sri Lanka (Leaflet, GeoJSON).
Secured patient data with AES-256 field-level encryption and blind indexes, HashiCorp Vault, OTP checks on record access and audit logs; added drug-interaction checks covering 191k+ pairs.
Cut the initial JS bundle from 465 KB to 145 KB with code-splitting; set up CI/CD with GitHub Actions and Vercel.

caseStudy.overview: MediSync is my BSc (Hons) Data Science capstone: a national healthcare platform for Sri Lanka that I designed and built on my own. It connects patients, doctors, pharmacies, hospitals/labs and administrators, keeps medical records encrypted, and forecasts disease outbreaks by district.
techDecisions: Split into three services (React 19 front end, Node.js/Express 5 API, Flask ML engine) so the Python forecasting work can scale and deploy independently of the web API.

Patient data is protected with AES-256 field-level encryption using an envelope-encryption flow. Keys are managed in HashiCorp Vault, and blind indexes let encrypted fields such as NIC numbers still be searched without decrypting them.
Outbreak detection combines Prophet forecasting with z-score anomaly detection, and the results appear on a public Sri Lanka district map built with Leaflet and GeoJSON.
Session tokens are kept in memory instead of localStorage to reduce XSS exposure, and patient records open only after an OTP check.
challenges: Upgrading to Express 5 broke express-mongo-sanitize and caused a site-wide outage. I traced it to the now read-only req.query, replaced the package with custom sanitising middleware, and learned to test dependencies against major-version upgrades.
The public health page was slow because one endpoint aggregated 20k+ rows on every request. Code-splitting cut the initial JS from 465 KB to 145 KB; caching that aggregation is the next step.
Finding secrets in the git history taught me to rotate credentials immediately and to add secret scanning and CI security tests (GitHub Actions) to the pipeline.

projects.summary: AI-driven national healthcare platform for Sri Lanka. Role-based portals, encrypted patient records and a public district map of outbreak risk, across React, Node.js and a Python ML service.

projects.name: Ayu Arana Care

projects.problem: A care home needs one place to manage residents, their medical records, memberships, payments and checkup requests, with staff only seeing what their role allows.
projects.solution: A MERN web app with role-based access control, resident medical records, membership tiers, payments and checkup requests, and a responsive React and Tailwind front end.
highlights: Role-based access control with bcrypt-hashed passwords.
Resident medical records and checkup requests.
cvBullets: Built a secure REST API in Node.js and Express with role-based access control and bcrypt, managing resident medical records, membership tiers and payments.

projects.name: Heart-disease prediction
projects.tagline: Comparing classic ML models and a neural network on the Cleveland UCI dataset
projects.role: Group coursework. The Random Forest, SVM and Logistic Regression comparison was the group part; the ANN was my individual component.
projects.problem: Predict the presence of heart disease from clinical measurements.
projects.solution: As a group we trained and compared Random Forest, SVM and Logistic Regression models on the Cleveland UCI heart-disease dataset. My individual component was an artificial neural network (ANN) for the same task.
projects.summary: Group comparison of Random Forest, SVM and Logistic Regression on the Cleveland UCI dataset; the ANN was my individual component.
